sign.title: Document Signing
sign.subtitle: Sign a document with your Radix wallet. The file never leaves your browser; only its hash is signed.

basic.hint: The simplest mode: drop the document and press Sign. Your wallet only receives the signing challenge (no name or email) and you download the signed file. No on-ledger anchoring; for multiple on-chain signers, anchoring or identity disclosure use the Advanced signing tab.

disclaimer.title: Before you sign
disclaimer.body: Your file is hashed locally and never uploaded. This proves integrity, timestamp and control of your account key, and the disclosed name is self-declared by your wallet, so it is not an identity-verified (qualified) electronic signature. On-chain data is public and permanent: only the hash is anchored, never the file, message or name.

connect.title: Connect your Radix wallet
connect.subtitle: You need a connected wallet to sign a document.

file.label: Document
file.prompt: Drop a file here or click to browse
file.ready: Hashed locally. The file stays on your device.

options.messageHint: A note bound into the signature. Kept off-chain.
options.identityHint: Choose which Persona details the certificate discloses. Email can be combined with any name option.
options.identityNoneDesc: Shares no data; shows your Persona
options.outputHint: What to download once signed. You can pick both.
options.outputDetachedDesc: A .radixsig.json next to your untouched file
options.outputEmbeddedDesc: A new PDF with the certificate inside
options.embeddedPdfOnly: Embedding is only available for PDF files.
options.anchorHint: Optionally mint a soulbound NFT holding the document hash.
options.anchorWarning: Only the hash is published on-ledger, public and permanent.
options.multiHint: Choose whether this document needs one signature or several.
options.coSignersHint: Leave empty to let anyone you send the certificate to sign. Or list accounts to require exactly those signers (they will get an error if they sign with a different account).
options.onchainSignersHint: List the accounts that must sign. Only those accounts will be able to: the list is recorded on-ledger when the request is created and cannot be changed afterwards.

steps.title: How signing with several people works (off-chain)
steps.s1: You sign the document first and download the certificate (.radixsig.json).
steps.s2: Send that certificate file AND the original document to the other signers.
steps.s3: Each person opens this tool, drops the original file and the certificate under “Co-sign”, and adds their signature.
steps.s4: They send the updated certificate back (or on to the next signer).
steps.s5: When everyone has signed, anyone can anchor it on-ledger from the result screen.

ledgerSteps.title: How multi-party signing works (on the ledger)
ledgerSteps.s1: You sign with your wallet and an invitation NFT is deposited into each required signer's account (or invitations only, if you choose not to sign yet).
ledgerSteps.s2: Share the link: it carries the right network, the document name and your output formats. If you keep the tab open, the document travels on its own over the direct browser-to-browser channel; you can also send the PDF with the request embedded.
ledgerSteps.s3: Each invitee opens the link, receives or uploads the document, the tool checks it matches the request's hash, and they sign from their wallet by minting their signature NFT.
ledgerSteps.s4: Status updates by reading the ledger. Once everyone has signed, anyone downloads the certificate or the signed PDF, verifiable without depending on this site.

cosign.title: Co-sign an existing certificate
cosign.hint: Were you sent a certificate to sign? Load it here to add your signature.
cosign.fileMismatch: This file does not match the certificate's document.

pdfInfo.title: Radix content embedded in the PDF
pdfInfo.originalRecovered: The original document travels inside the PDF: it was recovered and its hash is what gets checked.

progress.passToNext: Send this certificate to the remaining signers to complete it.

onboarding.title: Before signing on-ledger
onboarding.subtitle: Signing documents on-ledger needs two NFTs, one time only. After this step, this section disappears forever.
onboarding.sealBody: A non-transferable NFT you mint once from the official Radix Seal resource. It identifies you as a signer to anyone and is the ONLY key able to mint into your collection: without your Seal, nobody, not even this site, can create anything in your name. It can never be sold, moved or burned.
onboarding.collectionBody: Your personal on-ledger archive, reusable forever: every document you sign adds a numbered NFT (#1, #2, #3…) and every request you issue keeps its invitations there. Its rules are locked at creation: signatures are non-transferable, their data can never be edited, and only your Seal can mint. It works like your own self-custodied certificate authority: you issue, the ledger attests.
onboarding.invitesBody: When you request signatures from others, one invitation NFT per signer is minted, valid for that document only, and appears in each signer's wallet. Receiving an invitation never counts as signing: a signature is always the signer's own act in their own collection. As the issuer you can recall sent invitations; signatures, however, can never be touched by anyone.
onboarding.caNote: All of this is public and permanent on the Radix Network, and anyone can verify it without depending on this site.
onboarding.pointer: Complete the setup at the top (your Seal and your collection) to be able to sign on-ledger.

onchain.optionsLedgerNote: The message and identity disclosure don't apply when signing on the ledger: only the document hash is anchored.
onchain.onDesc: NFT invitations in the wallet; each signs from their own
onchain.sealMissing: The Seal is your personal insignia: a non-transferable NFT that identifies you as a signer and guards your collection. Minted once.
onchain.sealMinting: Confirm the seal in your wallet…
onchain.sealNotDeployed: The Radix Seal is not deployed on this network yet. Deploy it above (once per network) and reload.
onchain.sealWithCollection: Your Seal is minted automatically as the first step of creating your collection below.
onchain.collectionMissing: Your personal collection will hold the invitations you issue and your signatures across all documents. Only your Seal can mint into it.
onchain.collectionCreating: Confirm the collection in your wallet…
onchain.twoTxNote: You do not have a Seal yet, so this sends two transactions: first your soulbound Seal, then your collection. Approve both in your wallet, one after the other.
onchain.issuerHint: Name, website and logo are optional, get recorded into your collection's metadata, and are public and permanent.
onchain.requestHint: Each listed signer receives an invitation NFT in their wallet: a verifiable notice that THEY are asked to sign THIS document (its hash is engraved in it, so it is useless for any other file). Invitations exist so signers find out right in their wallet, so there is a public, unalterable record of who was asked to sign, and so the tool only counts signatures from invited accounts. An invitation signs nothing by itself: signing is always each person's own act from their own wallet. Sent the wrong address? You can recall an invitation; and if you pick "Sign and send", you are included as a signer too.
onchain.soloHint: Your signature is minted as an NFT into your personal collection, holding the document hash. Public, permanent and verifiable by anyone.
onchain.inviteSignDesc: Your signature and the invitations, in one transaction
onchain.inviteSendDesc: You send the invitations; you can sign later
onchain.needSigners: Add at least one required signer above.
onchain.invalidSigner: Account address not valid for this network
onchain.depositWarning: Invitations are deposited into the signers' accounts: if any account blocks deposits from strangers, the whole transaction fails.
onchain.requestDetected: This PDF carries an embedded on-ledger signing request: it was loaded automatically along with the original document.
onchain.requestFilePrompt: You have received an on-ledger signing request. Upload the original document (or the PDF you were sent) to check it matches the request and sign from your wallet.
onchain.invalidKey: The key does not look like a request key (resource_…:#1#).
onchain.dropFileToCompare: Upload the document above to check it matches the hash recorded on-ledger.
onchain.hashMatches: Your document matches the request's hash
onchain.shareTitle: Share this link with the signers
onchain.shareHint: Each signer received their invitation in their wallet; with this link (or the PDF) they open the request here and sign from their own wallet. The link carries the network and your output formats.
onchain.shareDocHint: Whoever opens this link while this tab stays open receives the signed document directly, browser to browser, end-to-end encrypted. They can verify it or add their signature.
onchain.qrAlt: QR code of the share link

onchain.sendToggleHint: While this tab stays open, whoever opens the link receives the document automatically, browser to browser, end-to-end encrypted. It never touches a server.

onchain.recvSignedHint: This document is signed by everyone required. It has been saved automatically; use the button if your browser blocked the download.
onchain.recvHint: The document arrives straight from the sender, end-to-end encrypted. You can sign it once it finishes.
onchain.downloadRequestPdf: Download PDF with the request embedded
onchain.downloadRequestPdfHint: A single self-describing file: it contains the original document and the request key. Anyone dropping it here sees the request loaded automatically.

onchain.notEligibleHint: Share the invited account from your wallet, or ask the issuer to create a new request that includes your account.
onchain.alreadySigned: You have already signed this document. Nothing left to do.

onchain.firstSignNote: This is your first signature: your personal collection is created together with it in the same transaction.

onchain.statusHint: Paste the signing-request key (or open the link you were sent) to see who has signed and who is still pending, read straight from the Radix Network. Neither the document nor the certificate is needed.
onchain.fileMismatch: The uploaded file does not match this request.

deploy.title: Deploy Radix Seal (one-time)
deploy.subtitle: The Radix Seal brand is not yet deployed on {network}. Deploy it once with your wallet.
deploy.imageUrlHint: Public URL of the seal image. With the admin badge you can change it later; use a stable, domain-independent URL (the GitHub SVG by default).
deploy.symbolHint: Short ticker for the brand resource, up to 5 letters/digits (e.g. SEAL). Uppercased automatically.
deploy.done: Radix Seal deployed. Copy the resource address below.
deploy.paste: Paste it into features/sign/constants/seal.ts → RADIX_SEAL for this network, then reload.
deploy.adminBadgeHint: The admin badge is a single NFT. With it, the brand metadata (name, image, description) will be editable only by whoever holds that badge, forever. Paste an existing badge resource address or mint a new one. Leave empty to make the brand immutable.
deploy.badgeReady: Admin badge NFT minted and in your account. Keep it safe (ideally in a multisig).

seal.title: Radix Seal
seal.hint: Your attestations mint into ONE reusable collection (a new #id per document), not a new resource each time. Customise how it appears in your wallet.
seal.imageUrlHint: Shown on the collection and each attestation in your wallet. Empty = the Radix Seal image.
seal.collectionStatusNew: First anchor: your Radix Seal collection will be created (id #1).
seal.watermarkHint: Optionally stamp the signed PDF. The original file is embedded intact for verification.

seal.watermarkImageHint: You can set text, an image, or both (if an image is set, the image is used). The image is processed in your browser and never uploaded to any server.

certificatePage.title: Signature Certificate
certificatePage.tagline: Self-custody signature on the Radix Network
certificatePage.selfDeclared: Name self-declared by the signer's wallet (not identity-verified)
certificatePage.pendingNote: This document is NOT fully signed yet. These required signers have not signed:
certificatePage.anchorNote: Public, permanent record on the Radix Network. Only the document hash and the accounts are on the ledger — never the file, the message or a name.
certificatePage.certNote: This document also carries a standard PDF digital signature. Your PDF reader validates this certificate against its own trusted authorities.
certificatePage.verifyInstruction: Scan the code or open the address below, then drop this PDF into the verifier. Verification runs in your browser and reads the public Radix ledger.
certificatePage.disclaimer: A Radix Seal signature proves the document's integrity, its timestamp, and control of the signing account. Any disclosed name is self-declared by the signer's wallet, so this is not an identity-verified qualified electronic signature (such as eIDAS QES). When anchored on the ledger it stays verifiable for as long as the Radix Network exists.

pades.title: Certificate signature (PAdES / X.509)
pades.hint: Optionally add a standard PDF digital signature with your own X.509 certificate, so Adobe/Foxit show it in their signatures panel. It complements the Radix proof; it does not replace it.
pades.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. I am the author of this document
pades.note: The signature is made in your browser with your certificate. The private key never leaves your device and is never uploaded. A self-signed certificate will show as untrusted until the recipient trusts it; legal recognition requires a certificate issued by a trusted CA.
pades.pdfOnly: Certificate signing needs the embedded PDF output.

errors.generic: Could not sign with the certificate.

verify.aboutBody: Upload the original file and its .radixsig.json certificate, or an embedded signed PDF that carries them, and verification runs automatically. The file is hashed locally and never uploaded: only the certificate is checked. It confirms the document hasn't been altered, that the wallet signatures are valid and, if present, its on-chain record. For an on-ledger signing you can also paste the request key (or open its link) and see who has signed, no certificate needed.
verify.fileMismatch: File does NOT match. It was altered
verify.onchainInvalid: On-ledger record could not be confirmed
verify.embeddedDetected: Certificate and original document read from the signed PDF.
verify.sealInvalid: Collection does not reference the official Radix Seal
verify.incomplete: Not all required signers have signed yet
verify.badCert: That file is not a valid certificate.
verify.clockNone: No independent clock: the date is only declared
verify.clockMismatch: The declared date does NOT match the independent clock
verify.clockUntrusted: Timestamping authority not recognised by this deployment
verify.declaredHeader: Declared, not covered by the signature
verify.declaredNote: In an on-ledger-only certificate the chain ties the signer to the document hash and to nothing else. The message, the name and the dates below come from whoever built the certificate.
verify.nameDeclared: A displayed name never goes on the ledger and no signature covers it: it is a declaration.
verify.requestFromKey: Required signers read from the key you entered
verify.requestFromCert: Required signers read from the request the certificate points at
verify.requestMismatch: The certificate points at a different request than the key you entered. Yours wins.
verify.clockIssuedAtMismatch: The signature NFT states a date other than that of its own transaction

intro.title: Your seal commands your collection
intro.body: Radix Seal works in two pieces: an insignia (the seal), which can neither be transferred nor burned, and a signing collection owned by that seal. Every invitation and every signature you issue is an NFT inside that collection, which is what makes an on-ledger signature attributable to your account. This is where you see and manage both.

connect.title: Connect your Radix Wallet
connect.subtitle: The collection belongs to your seal, so the wallet holding it is needed to view and manage it.

seals.title: Your seal
seals.hint: The soulbound insignia that commands your collections. It can never be transferred or burned.
seals.none: This account has no seal yet. One is minted automatically with your first collection, here or from Sign document.
seals.severalNote: This account holds more than one seal. Only the one commanding the active collection can sign into it; the rest sit inert, and since a seal cannot be burned, they stay.

list.title: Signing collections
list.hint: Where your invitations and signatures live. The active one is what Sign document and Encrypt use.
list.none: This account has no signing collection yet.
list.severalNote: You hold more than one collection. Invitations and signatures already issued stay in theirs: switching the active one does not move them, it only decides where the next ones are minted.

create.title: New signing collection
create.hint: Created in your seal's name, so only you can ever mint into it. The name and issuer identity can be changed later.
create.duplicateWarning: Careful: you already have a collection and you are about to create a second one. Every signature and invitation you have issued lives inside the collection you used at the time, and stays there: the new one starts empty. Anyone holding an invitation from you will keep seeing the old collection's name and logo, not the new one's. From now on you will sign from whichever you leave active. A second collection makes sense to keep identities apart: for example one collection to sign as an individual and another collection to sign as a company. The same goes if you run several companies: one collection per company, each with its own name and logo, so whoever receives a signature sees straight away on whose behalf it was signed.
create.noSealNote: This account has no seal insignia yet. The button below mints one first and creates the collection second: two wallet confirmations, back to back.
create.logoHint: Used as the collection's icon and as the seal insignia's image. Left empty, the Radix Seal image is used.
create.newSealHint: Its own insignia for this identity
create.reuseSealNote: The collection will belong to the insignia you already have, which can own several. A single wallet confirmation, and the logo is used only as the collection's icon.
create.newSealNote: A second insignia is minted with the logo you set and this collection will be its own. Since an insignia can never be transferred or burned, it stays in the account forever. Two wallet confirmations, back to back.
create.customHint: Key/value pairs written onto the collection, shown by wallets and explorers next to the rest. The keys the standard writes itself are not available (name, symbol, description, icon_url, tags, issuer, org_name, org_url, radix_seal, radix_sign_collection).
create.customLockHint: Once locked it can never be changed again, not even by you.
create.customReserved: The standard writes that key itself: pick another.

identity.title: Issuer identity
identity.hint: What someone receiving a signature from you sees. It lives on the active collection and changing it takes a signature from your seal.
identity.noCollection: You need an active collection to edit its identity. Create one in the next tab.
identity.logoHint: The collection icon; also used as the issuer logo
identity.lockedNote: Only these fields are editable. The description, the seal reference, the issuing account and every signature's own data were sealed when the collection was created and can never be touched, not even by you.

sign.title: Document Signing on Radix
sign.description: Sign documents with your Radix wallet. Files are hashed locally and never uploaded; optionally anchor the hash on-ledger as a soulbound NFT.
